title: Influence bound for randomized trees
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty alphabet with probability law $\pi$, and suppose the real-valued functions on $\Omega$ have a finite nonempty orthonormal basis for the $\pi$-weighted inner product that includes the constant-one function. For a randomized decision tree on $n$ coordinates and a function $f:(\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\Omega)\to\mathbb R$ taking only the values $-1$ and $1$, one half the sum over coordinates of the query probability times the product influence of $f$ is at least the smaller of the probabilities that $f$ equals $1$ and $-1$, minus the tree’s error probability.
hypotheses_covered: There is a finite nonempty index type with decidable equality
A basis indexed by that type is orthonormal for the $\pi$-weighted inner product and has a constant-one vector
The randomized tree has a finite nonempty seed space with a probability law
$f$ is a real-valued function on $n$-coordinate inputs
